claims.text: India and Uzbekistan upgraded their bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership during talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent.
India and Uzbekistan set an annual bilateral trade target of $5 billion by 2030.
PM Narendra Modi announced that India would enter into a long-term arrangement for the supply of uranium from Uzbekistan.
India and Uzbekistan agreed to establish a foreign minister-level coordination council to guide bilateral cooperation.
India and Uzbekistan signed 11 MoUs covering culture, education, mining, Ayurveda, tourism, and the restoration of Buddhist sites.
Annual trade between India and Uzbekistan stands at $1.32 billion.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred with Uzbekistan's Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order on August 30, 2026.
The Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order marks the 36th honorary award conferred upon Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2016.
Commerce ministry data shows bilateral trade between India and Uzbekistan stood at $1.3 billion in 2025, a 33.3% increase from the previous year.
Uzbekistan expressed appreciation for India's support regarding Uzbekistan's accession to the World Trade Organization.
Uzbekistan was the first stop in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's two-nation tour, which also includes a visit to Kyrgyzstan for the SCO Summit.
Sibi George, secretary (West) in the external affairs ministry, stated that India and Uzbekistan are closing in on signing an agreement for uranium supply very shortly.
President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced the introduction of a 30-day visa-free regime for Indian citizens.
India announced a grant of $1 million for afforestation initiatives in the Aral Sea region.
NPCI International Payments Ltd signed a commercial agreement with Uzbekistan's National Interbank Processing Centre JSC to allow Indian UPI apps to scan national QR codes in Uzbekistan.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Tashkent on August 29, 2026, for a two-day state visit.
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk stated on the Prakhar Gupta Xperience podcast that Cockroach Janta Party movement organisers appeared to have political ambitions, which he called normal.
Sonam Wangchuk advised CJP organizers to maintain the platform as a neutral, apolitical pressure group to retain supporter trust.
The Cockroach Janta Party movement led protests that resulted in the resignation of former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
The 1979 Assam student agitation led by AASU transformed into the Asom Gana Parishad political party, which formed the Assam government in 1985.
The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam party, led by C. Joseph Vijay, won and formed the government in Tamil Nadu in 2026.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke stated that the BJP believes it has grown bigger than the RSS.
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated in New York that if any Hindu thinks there should be no Muslims in Bharat, he will not remain a Hindu.
Abhijeet Dipke criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for describing protesting Gen Z individuals as 'Dimagi Naxal'.
On August 15, the Cockroach Janta Party launched a campaign organizing volunteer audits of government schools to document basic facilities.
The Cockroach Janta Party set an initial goal to audit 100 rural government schools over two months.
Education Ministry data shows India has over one million government schools, accounting for nearly 70% of all schools while serving under half of the country's 247 million students.
Authorities in Maharashtra and Rajasthan objected to CJP school audits conducted without prior official permission.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath ordered on-the-spot checks of school facilities and directed police to register cases over misleading school videos.
Retired Delhi Police officer Rajendra Singh filed a petition in the Supreme Court seeking restrictions on unpermitted marches in Lutyens' Delhi.
The Cockroach Janta Party announced plans for a September 5 protest march from India Gate to Delhi Police Headquarters.
The Supreme Court petition requests postponing or regulating organized demonstrations in Lutyens' Delhi until after the BRICS Summit scheduled for September 12-13.
